chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Muthanna ibn Rashid, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about an orphan who has recited the Quran, and there is nothing wrong with his intellect, and he has wealth in the hands of a man. So the man who holds the wealth wanted to do business with the orphan's wealth on a profit-sharing basis (mudarabah). So the boy permitted him in that. He (the Imam) said: 'It is not correct that he works with it until he reaches puberty (ihtilam) and hands over his wealth to him.' He said: 'And if he were to reach puberty and there was not intellect for him, nothing would be handed over to him ever.'
Humayd, from al-Hasan, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), similar to that.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for an orphan to take possession of their wealth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia juristic distinction between biological maturity (bulugh) and financial competence (rushd), establishing that puberty alone does not grant an orphan full control over their wealth. It highlights that even if an orphan is physically mature, a lack of sound intellect (aql) or guidance prevents the transfer of assets, ensuring their financial protection until they demonstrate sufficient discernment to manage their estate.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from one of his companions, from Masny Bin Rashid, from Abu Baseer,

(The narrator says): ‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about an orphan who has read the Quran, and there is nothing wrong with his intellect. And for him is wealth in the hands of a man. So the man wanted to do some business with the wealth of the orphan which was with him on a profit-sharing basis. So the boy permitted him with regards to that’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not correct that he works with it until he (the orphan) bed-wets and hands over his wealth to him. And if he were to bed-wet and there does not happen to be intellect for him, nothing would be handed over to him (the businessman), ever’.

Humeyd, from Al Hassan, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, from Dawood Bin Sirhan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, similar to that’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Sama‘ah from certain persons of his people from Muthanna’ ibn Rashid from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of an orphan who has read the Quran, his understanding is proper and his assets are in the hands of a man who wants to work using those assets in business in the manner of profit sharing ( al-Mudarabah ) to which the boy has agreed. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not proper to use it in business until he experiences wet-dream, then hands over his assets to him. If he experiences wet-dream and does not have proper understanding, nothing must be given to him forever.’”
Humayd has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ja‘far ibn Sama‘ah from Dawud ibn Sarhan from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, a similar Hadith.
